title: Il numero unico: 112
summary: Emergency phrases and Italy's single emergency number, 112

blocks.title: Il numero unico: 112
blocks.body: For any real emergency in Italy, call **il 112** — the single European emergency number. Tell the operator **cosa è successo** (what happened) and **dove ti trovi** (where you are); they route you to the ambulance, police, or fire brigade as needed. You don't need to guess the right number — 112 covers it all.
blocks.callout: One number for everything: 112. Say what happened, then where you are.

blocks.title: Frasi per l'emergenza
blocks.body: A handful of set phrases worth knowing by heart: *Ho bisogno di aiuto* (I need help), *C'è stato un incidente* (There's been an accident), *Chiami un'ambulanza, per favore* (Call an ambulance, please — the polite way of asking a stranger). You'll meet the grammar behind that last one properly later; for now, just learn it as a ready-made phrase.
blocks.callout: Learn these whole, ready to use — the grammar catches up later.

blocks.prompt: What number do you dial for any emergency in Italy?
blocks.explain: 112 is the single European emergency number — it works everywhere in Italy (and the EU).
*C'è stato un incidente* — the passato prossimo of c'è, for something that just happened.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.

blocks.scene: Out with Marco, 'You' start feeling a sharp pain — Marco decides whether it's 112-worthy

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Marco, non mi sento bene. Ho un forte dolore al petto.
lines.en: Marco, I don't feel well. I have a sharp pain in my chest.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Un dolore al petto? Non scherziamo, chiamo subito il 112.
lines.en: Chest pain? No joking around, I'm calling 112 right now.
lines.spotlight: Marco doesn't hesitate — chest pain is exactly what 112 is for, not the farmacia.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Aspetta, magari è solo il caffè di oggi…
lines.en: Wait, maybe it's just today's coffee…

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Meglio controllare. In un'emergenza è sempre meglio chiamare.
lines.en: Better to check. In an emergency it's always better to call.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Pronto? Sì, una persona con un forte dolore al petto — siamo in Via Mazzini.
lines.en: Hello? Yes, a person with a sharp chest pain — we're on Via Mazzini.

lines.speaker: You
lines.en: Thanks, Marco. Better safe than sorry.

questions.q: What does Marco decide to do right away?
